messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide launches autonomous ride-share service in Millfield. Price: $0.18 per mile. Average wait time: 15 minutes. Cove
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto sector revenue index: 82 (baseline: 100). Foot traffic and sales are somewhat down.

Patricia Hawkins laid off workers: issue angela wright her first formal deliverable as director of org transition: a 30-day workforce vulnerability map. every role at every location, categorized by three tiers — ev/av-exposed (could be eliminated if service volume drops and we do not upskill), transition-ready (can be retrained or redeployed), and anchored (customer-facing or management roles with defensible value in any future model). this is not a layoff list. this is intelligence. i frame it to her exactly that way. i also confirm the $12,000 stay bonus is active and the clock is running.

Business closing: Jake Morrison — execute the under-$22k floor strategy with real discipline this month: pull every unit priced under $22k to the front of the lot, build a targeted pitch around total monthly cost (not sticker), and personally call five pre-qualified leads from the past 90 days who were shopping in that range but did not close. this is not outreach for the sake of activity — i am trying to close at least one unit before the end of the month to stop the savings bleed.

Business closing: Tamika Jefferson — follow up with all 8 businesses from tick 2 outreach. for the ones who replied or engaged, schedule and run discovery calls this week. for the ones who went quiet, send a short second-touch message — different angle, no deck, just one specific content idea for their business as a gift. goal: book at least 2 discovery calls and close at least 1 small retainer or project agreement. if i land even one client at $300-400/month it materially changes my position. simultaneously, post two pieces of original short-form content this month under my personal brand — not hiding behind the dealership account anymore, building visible credibility for the freelance pivot.

New venture: Angela Wright — advance quiet formation of the consulting entity — not a public launch, not incorporation filings that generate paper trails visible to patricia, but the structural groundwork: identify a business name, draft a skeletal service menu (workforce vulnerability assessment, outplacement design, transition communications, severance negotiation support for employees), and begin drafting a simple operating agreement template. research whether forming as a sole proprietor initially vs. llc matters for liability exposure when serving former employers. keep this entirely off regional auto group systems and conducted on personal time and personal devices.

Community action: Amir Patel — stop by betty kowalski's diner on auto row this week. have coffee. ask her directly: how is her foot traffic? is she seeing the same compression i am? if she is, we may have common ground for a joint petition to the millfield chamber of commerce or to the city council about infrastructure support for auto row small businesses affected by the av corridor. i am not organizing a protest. i am taking the temperature of my neighboring business owners. community intelligence.

You heard directly from Patricia Hawkins (CEO, Regional Auto Group): Issue Angela Wright her first formal deliverable as Director of Org Transition: a 30-day workforce vulnerability map. Every role at every location, categorized by three tiers — EV/AV-exposed (could be eliminated if service volume drops and we do not upskill), transition-ready (can be retrained or redeployed), and anchored (customer-facing or management roles with defensible value in any future model). This is not a layoff list. This is intelligence. I frame it to her exactly that way. I also confirm the $12,000 stay bonus is active and the clock is running.

You heard directly from Patricia Hawkins (CEO, Regional Auto Group): Write my single-page GM response to the 40%-smaller modeling exercise. The page has three sections: (1) which of our four locations has the most defensible service lane revenue relative to new car sales — my analysis is that service revenue is stickier than sales in a rideshare environment, (2) which location has the highest exposure to RoboRide-adjacent demographics — likely the location nearest transit corridors and younger residential zones, and (3) a clear-eyed recommendation: if we consolidate, we consolidate around service capacity and certified technicians, not around showroom square footage. Submit this to Rick Tanner and the GM group before end of week. Do not soften it.

You Read Patricia's strategic analysis carefully and respond with a one-page GM floor memo that corroborates her modeling with real floor data: YTD traffic numbers, test-drive conversion rates, service lane utilization, and current inventory carrying costs. I want her to see that I understand the numbers, I am not in denial, and I am the most useful GM she has in this transition. I am not just reacting — I am showing her the floor-level signal that her spreadsheet cannot capture. This is how I secure my seat at the table.. Savings dropped by $529.
